concepts.name: Support and Resistance
concepts.definition: Price areas where buying or selling interest has repeatedly appeared, used to frame entries, exits and stops.

concepts.name: Trend
concepts.definition: The prevailing direction of price, usually read from the sequence of higher highs and higher lows (or the reverse). Trading with it keeps momentum on your side.

concepts.name: Opening Range
concepts.definition: The high and low of the first few minutes of the session. A break of either side is often used as a trigger or as context for the day.

concepts.name: Position Sizing
concepts.definition: Choosing how many shares or contracts to trade so that a stopped-out trade costs a small, predefined amount of the account.

concepts.name: Stop Loss
concepts.definition: A predefined exit price that caps the loss on a trade. It is set before entry, based on where the idea is proven wrong.

concepts.name: Risk / Reward
concepts.definition: The ratio between the amount risked on a trade and the amount targeted. Favourable ratios let a modest win rate stay profitable.

concepts.name: Overtrading
concepts.definition: Taking more trades than the plan calls for, often out of boredom, frustration or a wish to win back losses.

concepts.name: Journaling
concepts.definition: Recording each trade, the reasoning behind it and how it went, then reviewing the record to find repeatable mistakes and strengths.
